stem: For more than 6 months, a client has had one or more distressing physical symptoms that disrupt daily life and are accompanied by persistent excessive health-related thoughts, anxiety, and time devoted to the symptoms. Which disorder is most consistent with this presentation?

options.A: Malingering, which involves intentional symptom production for an external incentive
options.B: Factitious disorder, which involves intentional falsification without an obvious external reward
options.C: Illness anxiety disorder, which is characterized by preoccupation with serious illness despite absent or only mild somatic symptoms
options.D: Somatic symptom disorder, which involves distressing symptoms plus excessive symptom-related thoughts, feelings, or behaviors

rationale: Somatic symptom disorder requires one or more distressing somatic symptoms that cause significant disruption, excessive symptom-related thoughts, feelings, or behaviors, and persistence of the symptomatic state, typically for more than 6 months. The symptoms do not have to be medically unexplained and are not intentionally fabricated. D is therefore the only option that matches the complete pattern.
educational_objective: Differentiate somatic symptom disorder from illness anxiety disorder, factitious disorder, and malingering using symptom burden, excessive health concern, persistence, and intentionality/external incentive.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (SAMHSA DSM-5 criteria table; StatPearls)

source_claim_supported: Somatic symptom disorder includes distressing/disruptive somatic symptoms, excessive symptom-related thoughts/feelings/behaviors, and persistent symptomatic status typically longer than 6 months; symptoms may or may not be medically explained.

source_original.stem: A client has one or more distressing physical symptoms plus persistent excessive health-related thoughts, anxiety, or time devoted to the symptoms, causing major disruption in daily life. Which disorder is most consistent with this presentation?

options.A: Malingering, in which symptoms are intentionally produced for a clear external incentive or gain
options.B: Factitious disorder, in which illness is intentionally falsified without an obvious external reward
options.C: Illness anxiety disorder, in which concern about illness occurs with absent or only mild symptoms
options.D: Somatic symptom disorder, in which distressing symptoms are accompanied by excessive health concerns

source_original.rationale: Somatic symptom disorder is defined by distressing somatic symptoms plus excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to those symptoms. The diagnosis does not require the symptoms to be medically unexplained and does not imply intentional fabrication.
source_original.source_detail: Somatic symptom disorder: distressing symptoms plus excessive related thoughts/feelings/behaviors; medically unexplained symptoms are not required; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Added the DSM persistence criterion (typically >6 months), retained the medically-explained/not-explained neutrality, and replaced the non-specific APA DSM landing-page locator with exact NCBI DSM-5 criteria and StatPearls locators. Reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the completed criterion set makes the distinction direct.

audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI DSM-5 criteria table plus StatPearls; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: NCBI criteria table remains consistent with the 2026 StatPearls edition page; no conflicting current criterion source identified on 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Distressing somatic symptoms, excessive symptom-related cognition/anxiety/time, persistence typically >6 months, and lack of a requirement for medically unexplained symptoms are directly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Malingering requires intentional production tied to external incentive.
distractor_audit.B: Factitious disorder requires intentional falsification/induction without obvious external reward.
distractor_audit.C: Illness anxiety disorder generally has absent or mild somatic symptoms and centers on fear/preoccupation with serious illness.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Adding >6 months and clinically significant disruption makes D uniquely defensible; C is excluded by prominent distressing somatic symptoms.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed no-answer cues beyond criterion-level distinctions; alternatives remain parallel diagnostic contrasts.
audit_findings.blueprint: Mental-health recognition and differentiation fits Psychosocial Integrity.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked NCBI Table 3.31 and StatPearls; the original item omitted duration, so the corrected stem was necessary before FINAL_QA_PASS.
